correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a fixed lifetime value gives the denominator as the expectation of one minus an exponential factor and the numerator as the mean lifetime minus that denominator divided by the inspection rate. Factoring out the positive-lifetime probability gives the stated formula. Dominated convergence recovers the conditional positive mean from the high-rate limit, and algebra then recovers the entire Laplace transform. Uniqueness of Laplace transforms proves identification, while the exact cancellation of the positive-mass probability proves the zero-atom blind spot. The bundled checker independently verifies reconstruction and zero-inflation invariance.

value.rationale: The source presents the rate-indexed random-inspection MRL as a sensitivity-analysis object. The theorem shows that the full population curve is much more informative: for positive lifetimes it is lossless for the entire lifetime distribution, while on the nonnegative class it has exactly one structural blind direction, zero inflation. This gives a complete identifiability classification with a direct interpretation for the source's empirical profile and clarifies what information can and cannot be encoded by varying the monitoring intensity.
